runs.title: USS Doris Miller: will the Navy rename it?
runs.prompt: There were recent reports that the US Navy might rename the aircraft carrier USS Doris Miller (which honors the Pearl Harbor hero) to honor Donald Trump instead. Find out what the Navy has actually decided: has the name been changed, and what, in the Navy's own words or the family's words, is the current status? Prefer an official or well-sourced statement over paywalled coverage. Start from Military.com and CNN.
runs.answer: The name has NOT been changed. In a statement Friday (Nov. 20, 2026) to CNN and USNI News, a spokesperson for acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao said: "There is no intention to change the name of the USS Doris Miller." The future Ford-class carrier CVN-81 remains USS Doris Miller, and Newport News Shipbuilding will lay its ceremonial keel on Dec. 5, 2026 — two days before the 85th anniversary of Pearl Harbor. Miller's great-nephew Thomas Bledsoe welcomed the decision, saying "Doris Miller's story is not just our family's history; it is American history. His courage deserves to be remembered, honored, and recognized for generations to come." Caveat: the Navy's statement did not address earlier reports (CNN, Aug. 20, 2026) that it had internally considered renaming the ship for Trump; the reports prompted letters from 73 House members and bills from Sen. Cory Booker and Rep. Debbie Dingell to protect the name.

Per that ESPN feed: Arizona is preparing veteran Josh Johnson to start Sunday vs. the Chiefs, with rookie Carson Beck dealing with back spasms, as coach Mike LaFleur said Friday ("proceeding as if Josh Johnson will start") — so Johnson is the expected starter, not an officially locked-in one.
obstacles: Article page returns HTTP 202 with no readable text (bot challenge) on every ESPN HTML URL tried: .com, .co.uk, m.espn.com, bare story ID, and /espn/print
ESPN JSON API returns headline/description only; the full story body is truncated out behind large video/image metadata blocks
No byline or full quotes could be verified from the article itself
